:::info

La documentación de esta integración la escribe su autor y, por ahora, solo está disponible en inglés.

:::

This integration follows **your SNCF trains in real time** in Gladys: the next departures of your trips (home → work, the way back…), their **delays**, the **cancellations** and their cause. It turns them into devices, scene triggers ("my train is cancelled", "my train leaves in 15 minutes") and dashboard widgets.

The data comes from the **official SNCF API**: real time for TGV INOUI, OUIGO, Intercités, TER, Lyria and Eurostar. **Transilien** trains are timetable only (no delays, no cancellations).

> Community integration, not affiliated with or endorsed by SNCF.

## Configuration

### 1. Get an API key (free)

1. Open the SNCF [developer token](https://numerique.sncf.com/startup/api/token-developpeur/) page.
2. Fill in your first name, last name and email, accept the terms of use.
3. The key (a 36-character identifier, like `0f1e2d3c-4b5a-…`) arrives by email.

The free key allows **5 000 requests a day**. The integration counts them itself and slows down before the limit: past it, the SNCF blocks the key for hours.

### 2. Fill in the integration

| Field               | Role                                                                                  |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **API key**         | required                                                                              |
| **Trip 1, 2, 3**    | departure and arrival stations (only **direct trains** are followed)                  |
| **Travel window**   | optional, e.g. `07:00-09:30`: the trains leaving in that window                       |
| **Travel days**     | optional, e.g. Monday to Friday (empty: every day)                                    |
| **Trains followed** | how many next trains per trip (4 by default)                                          |
| **Delay threshold** | from how many minutes a train counts as "delayed" (5 by default)                      |
| **Refresh**         | every 3 minutes around the window, every 30 minutes the rest of the time (by default) |

For a station, type:

- its **name**: "Rennes", "Lyon Part Dieu", "Paris Montparnasse" — the first result of the SNCF search is kept;
- its **UIC code**: "87471003";
- its **identifier**: "stop_area:SNCF:87471003".

When the name does not give the right station, use the **Find a station** button: it lists the matching stations with their identifier, to copy into the trip field.

Save, then click **Test the connection**: for each trip, it tells how many trains were found and the time of the next one.

#### The travel window

With a travel window, the integration follows the trains of the **next window**: today's while it is not over, then the next travel day's. In the evening, the widget already shows tomorrow morning's trains, and a cancellation announced the evening before fires your scene the evening before.

It also reads the API often **only around the window** (from an hour before to its end), which saves the quota: about 250 requests a day for a trip with a 2.5-hour window, 800 without a window.

### 3. Add the devices

In the **Discovery** tab, each trip shows up as a device "SNCF – _from_ → _to_". Add it and put it in a room. Widgets and scenes also work without the device, but choosing the trip in their settings goes through the device list.

| Feature                     | Value                                                               |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Next train**              | text, e.g. "07:42 · TER 858311 · +5 min" or "… · cancelled"         |
| **Delay of the next train** | in minutes, the one of the next train that runs (0 when on time)    |
| **Disrupted trains**        | how many followed trains are late (from the threshold) or cancelled |

## Scenes

### Triggers

| Trigger                      | When                                                                                  | Filters           |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| **SNCF: train delayed**      | a followed train becomes late (from the threshold), then again past 15 and 30 minutes | trip, delay level |
| **SNCF: train cancelled**    | a followed train is cancelled, or no longer stops at a station of the trip            | trip              |
| **SNCF: train leaving soon** | a followed train leaves in 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 45 or 60 minutes                        | trip, minutes     |

**Leaving soon** counts on the **real-time** departure: when your 7:42 train is 5 minutes late, "leaves in 15 minutes" comes at 7:32, not 7:27.

Every trigger provides variables: trip, train number and type, direction, date, scheduled and expected times, delay, cause, and a **summary** ready to send. Each event fires **once per train**, even after a restart of the integration.

### Action

**SNCF: next trains** gives the next train of a trip (times, delay, status, cause, minutes until departure, number of disrupted trains) and a sentence summarizing the following ones.

## Widgets

| Widget              | Content                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **SNCF trip**       | the next departure time and the time left, then each train with an on time / +N min / cancelled badge; tap a disrupted train to read the cause |
| **SNCF departures** | the departures board of a station, every direction: a station typed in the widget settings, or the departure station of a trip                 |

## Limits

- Only **direct trains** are followed (no change).
- **Transilien**: timetable only, no delays and no cancellations (a limit of the SNCF API).
- The **platform** is not provided by the official API.
- A cancelled train vanishes from the real-time data of the SNCF: the integration finds it by comparing with the timetable, then confirms it on the departures board of the station. When it cannot be confirmed, the train stays shown as scheduled rather than wrongly announced as cancelled.

## Troubleshooting

| Message                                 | What to do                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| "The SNCF API key is refused"           | check the key copied from the email (no space)                                                   |
| "Station not found: …"                  | use the **Find a station** button and copy the identifier it gives                               |
| "Daily quota of the SNCF API reached"   | the SNCF blocked the key until the time shown: fewer trips without a window, or longer intervals |
| "No train found in the followed period" | no direct train in the travel window: check the stations and the window, or empty it             |

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que SNCF te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SNCF API key | `section` | No | The trains come from the official SNCF API: TER, TGV INOUI, OUIGO, Intercités, Lyria, Eurostar… in real time (Transilien: timetable only, no delays). The key is free: fill in the form of the SNCF developer page, the key arrives by email. It allows 5 000 requests a day; the integration counts them and slows down before the limit. |
| API key | `secret` | Sí | The key received by email (a UUID, 36 characters). |
| Trip 1 | `section` | No | A station name ("Rennes", "Lyon Part Dieu"), its UIC code ("87471003") or the identifier given by the "Find a station" button ("stop_area:SNCF:87471003"). Only direct trains are followed. The travel window and days are optional: with them, the trains of the next window are followed and the API is read often only around it (it saves the daily quota). |
| Departure station | `string` | No |  |
| Arrival station | `string` | No |  |
| Travel window | `string` | No | Departures between these times, e.g. 07:00-09:30. Empty: the next trains, all day. |
| Travel days | `multi_select` | No | Empty: every day. |
| Trip 2 (optional) | `section` | No | Same fields as trip 1, for example the way back. Leave empty when unused. |
| Departure station | `string` | No |  |
| Arrival station | `string` | No |  |
| Travel window | `string` | No | Departures between these times, e.g. 07:00-09:30. Empty: the next trains, all day. |
| Travel days | `multi_select` | No | Empty: every day. |
| Trip 3 (optional) | `section` | No | Same fields as trip 1, for example the way back. Leave empty when unused. |
| Departure station | `string` | No |  |
| Arrival station | `string` | No |  |
| Travel window | `string` | No | Departures between these times, e.g. 07:00-09:30. Empty: the next trains, all day. |
| Travel days | `multi_select` | No | Empty: every day. |
| Settings | `section` | No | With a travel window, a trip costs about 250 requests a day with the default values; without one, about 800. Three trips and an open departures board stay within the 5 000 a day. |
| Trains followed per trip | `number` | No | The next trains of each trip, between 1 and 8. |
| Delay threshold (min) | `number` | No | From how many minutes a train counts as delayed (scenes, disrupted trains, colors). |
| Refresh around the window (min) | `number` | No | From an hour before the travel window to its end (all day without a window), between 2 and 30 minutes. |
| Refresh the rest of the time (min) | `number` | No | Outside the window (and at night), between 10 and 180 minutes. |

## Cómo instalar SNCF en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: SNCF aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/william-de71/gladys-sncf:1.0.0`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-sncf](https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-sncf).

SNCF requiere Gladys `>=5.1.1`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

SNCF es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [William-De71](https://github.com/William-De71), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
